comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C5-C7, C52-C53 regarding transcriptomic and proteomic evidence of exosome-associated gene upregulation upon β-catenin silencing. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with high confidence, citing multiple omics approaches and convergent evidence.

Complete concordance on claims C8-C16 demonstrating increased exosome secretion upon mutated β-catenin depletion. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers specifically praising the multidisciplinary approach including TIRF microscopy, NTA, TEM, and western blot techniques.

Strong agreement on claims C17-C22 showing consistent effects across multiple cell lines. OpenEval focuses on multi-cell line validation and correlation analyses; peer review emphasizes the compelling link between oncogenic β-catenin and downregulation of SDC4/RAB27A. Peer review also includes C27 in their evaluation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C23-C26 regarding GSK3 inhibition as gain-of-function validation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes multiple complementary readouts; peer reviewers explicitly praise the use of CHIR99021 in Huh7 cells as convincing corroborating evidence. OpenEval includes C27 while peer review does not.

Perfect agreement on claims C28-C31, C38, C59 linking β-catenin-mediated exosome regulation to immune cell infiltration. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes spheroid model limitations; peer reviewers describe the evidence as convincing, with Rab27a rescue experiment providing strong mechanistic support.

Complete concordance on claims C32-C36 validating findings in human patient samples using TCGA and Boyault cohorts. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes potential variability from different IHC cohorts; peer reviewers emphasize this as crucial clinical correlation with implications for immuno-oncologic therapy.

Perfect agreement on claims C37, C51, C69 representing main conclusions. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive multi-level evidence; peer reviewers unanimously affirm novelty and significance, with editor noting fundamental insights into β-catenin's role in intercellular communication via EVs.

Complete concordance on claims C1-C4, C39-C50 providing background context. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-cited background establishing clinical significance of HCC and CTNNB1 mutations; peer reviewers accept these as accurate representations of the field without question.

Agreement on claims C70-C72 regarding speculative future applications. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting biomarker utility and therapeutic potential require validation; peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing translational implications as reasonable extrapolations though untested. Slight divergence in confidence level.

Agreement on claims C54-C58 (OpenEval) and C55-C58 (peer review) regarding mechanistic gaps. Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes promoter analysis data not shown and mechanism remains speculative; peer reviewers view this as reasonable limitation for future work rather than current weakness.

Strong agreement on claims C60-C67 discussing EV biology complexity. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for appropriately acknowledging contradictory findings; peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, noting well-cited context. OpenEval includes C68 (EV content investigation needed) while peer review addresses C68 separately in R8.

Both address claim C68 regarding need to investigate β-catenin-regulated EV content. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for acknowledging this gap; peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 identifying this as key limitation since conclusions assume immune evasion based solely on exosome quantity, not composition differences.

Agreement on claims C73-C76 (OpenEval) and C74-C76 (peer review) providing additional system characterization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes β-catenin presence in EVs is well-documented; peer reviewers accept these as part of convincing and robust characterization data.

Agreement on claims C77-C79 documenting control experiments. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these validate the experimental system and rule out cytotoxicity; peer reviewers specifically praise well-designed control experiments showing no viability effects.

Agreement on claims C80-C82 providing validation experiments. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these demonstrate effects are not due to off-target effects; peer reviewers accept multi-cell line validation as part of robust experimental design and complementary lines of investigation.
